Half Life Alyx is the half-life game I didn't know I wanted. This game sets the bar for story driven VR. My first play through took 13 hours but little is filler. Each level felt fresh. There are certain chapters that could be spun off as an entire game (looking at you, point extraction).

I highly recommend the Valve Index gloves when using Half life alyx. The game seamlessly (except in a handful of situations. There's one in particular in Breaking and Entering) uses the grip detection to pick up / grab / pull / or push things in the world. You can forget you are using a controller at all. I also love how the game punishes you for not ducking behind cover in fire fights.

For those new to the half life franchise - you'll love it. For those waiting for episode 3 - It may be disappointing (at first), but you should still give it a shot.

Conclusion: Thumbs up.

HL:A is a good game. However, it has some severe performance issues. It's not that it requires a powerful GPU to run, but you need 8 GB of VRAM at minimum to have a somewhat decent experience. With my RTX 2070 Super and Quest 2 connected with Air Link, whenever I'm in a large open area there are severe frame drops.
If your graphics card has 6 GB of VRAM or less, give this game a hard pass until you get a card with more.

This game gives me hope and wonder for how amazing VR can be. I'm poor and play on an o.g. Vive but still, the textures and lighting are breathtaking. There are times I literally stop and just look at wires or pipes, run my hand over a surface. The mechanics take the best, (or at least very good) from the platform and do it well.

The game play itself is really cool. Good story, good mixture of environments and puzzles vs active enemies. One minute you're laughing and the next you're terrified and trying to reload while being chased. Anyone who doesn't know why we need more than 10 round magazines has obviously never been in the zombie apocalypse. I wish it had co-op but even alone, it's really fun. I'm definitely not knocking it but it's like everything that Arizona Sunshine could have been. Of course they are a small team and came out way earlier but I'd love to play that with Alyx's level of detail and interactivity.

Get it on sale or if it's within your means, get it full price. You won't be let down. I can't wait to see what comes after this. Or even this with a better headset/display. (I do love my Vive)

If for some god-forsaken reason you still haven't played it yet, you absolutely should play it right now if you have a pulse and a VR headset.
Valve pulled no punches. Half-Life has always been on the bleeding edge of technology, and HLA is no exception. (both HL1 and HL2 were extremely demanding games when they released, and even HLA isn't great on the lower end of the VR spectrum.)
Every single minute of this game is incredible. and I do mean every single minute. There was not a single part of the game that I didn't enjoy. (although some parts were definitely better than others).
That being said, it's not really a game you play more than a few times. It's not particularly difficult (this was intentional; HLA is designed to be someone's first introduction to VR) and large-scale modding projects have yet to bear fruit (at time of writing).
At the very least you should play it just for the ending (if you still somehow haven't been spoiled on it yet).
No. Seriously. Stop looking at reviews. Just buy it. You're witnessing a new era of gaming come to life, and it's one that I'm overjoyed to be apart of.

A masterpiece that shows what vr games could be. The VR controls are smooth and responsive with the gravity gloves in particular being so intuitive and easy to use. I was honestly surprised how natural it felt to just be flicking things to myself after only a few minutes with the gloves.
The object interaction in Half-life alyx surpasses most vr games out there where you can actually rummage through desks full of objects. The shooting controls is very good and the weapon upgrade system was well thought out to complement the vr.
The story and story telling is great, each level I was in, I had a pretty good idea of what was happening and what I needed to do. The level designs are also very intuitive and they made sure they made full use of what vr. Each level feels distinct and memorable for the most part.
With great voicework, animations and details in the environments to make things actually feel alive, Half life alyx is by far the most immersive vr game I have played to date.

Not that anyone Care's but the OrangeBox started my interest in 3D art as a whole, Modding in the source engine was my first step into the art world. I spent years thinking Game development was like magic... Unattainable and something i'd never understand, but as I Do 3D art and work on my VR game with a friend I'm reminded that it's Valves Craftsmanship that made me even care about Art and Games in the first place.... With that out of the way Half-life as a series holds a special place in my Heart, obsessing over easter-eggs and lore and playing the games on repeat many times. Alyx Exceeded anything I could've hoped for.... after 14 years, and being in a dark place for much of that time, when the Half-life: Alyx trailer dropped it convinced me that there are a few things I want to see happen before I give up... and if Valve could make a game again after all these years maybe some other seemingly impossible things could happen in my life. This is less of a Review and more of a Note to the Talented people at Valve saying that this game means a lot to me and even Helped me stay around a little while longer.
-Thank you Valve I look forward to your future games

Incredible atmosphere, graphics, physics... but I have to say that I'm a bit disappointed with the overall interactivity the player has with the environment.

It's really frustating not being able to use the scene's items as improvised weapons (there aren't even melee weapons) or having to select through the hand controller the weapon do you want to use instead of grabbing them directly from your body; that means selected weapons will be sticked to your hand even if you don't press the common grab button.
This both features were implemented way after release of HL: Alyx by INDIE games as Pavlov, Boneworks or Blade & Sorcery.

I recommend playing it, it's a really enjoyable game, but the lack of real interactivity, not just moving, grabbing and throwing objects (WOW!), really frustrates me.

One of the best VR experiences. Immersive and atmospheric, *Alyx* transports you into the Half-Life universe. The game explores various types of environments, encourages exploration of the interactive setting with resource gathering, features finely-tuned VR mechanics, and boasts beautifully crafted and well-designed environments. At the same time, it’s not exhausting, keeping your curiosity for exploration alive and offering a comfortable duration for a VR game.
Recommended for anyone seeking an excellent VR experience.
